hdmi_rx.description: An HDMI/DVI receiver: a TMDS link in, parallel video out -- pixel clock, lock, data enable, syncs, 24 data bits. Every implementation offers these same ports, so the bayerlink receiver and the designs above it do not change when it does. How it is configured on a board, and which pins it lands on, is that board's.

link_khz.description: The link's pixel clock, in kHz: the rate the source sends, which the implementation's clocking is set for.

inputs.name: TMDS
inputs.description: The link, from the jack's pins.

inputs.name: refclk
inputs.description: The reference clock the implementation calibrates its input delays with; its frequency is the implementation's fact refclk_mhz.

outputs.name: pclk
outputs.description: The clock recovered from the link: it stops when the cable is pulled.

dvi2rgb.description: Digilent's dvi2rgb on a 7-series part: TMDS decoded in the fabric (ISERDESE2, IDELAYE2, an MMCM). Needs Digilent's vivado-library in the IP catalogue. Lane map solved 2026-08-12 on a PYNQ-Z2 with the picam2hdmi source, counting and checker patterns: it follows this IP's bus order, not the board, so it holds on any board receiving through dvi2rgb. kClkRange follows the link: its MMCM multiplies the link clock by 5 x kClkRange and divides by kClkRange, so the five-times serial clock is the same whatever the range, and the range only keeps the VCO inside its 600-1200 MHz specification -- range 1 at a 74.25 MHz link would run it at 371 MHz. Range 2 at 74.25 MHz judged 30/30 frames bit-exact on the PYNQ-Z2 (2026-10-09). Below 25 MHz it has no range.

config.kClkRange: 1 if link_khz >= 120000 else 2 if link_khz >= 60000 else 3 if link_khz >= 40000 else 4 if link_khz >= 30000 else 5
